Only methods declared in sugar-animation/src, or inherited from a parent declared there, are listed. A type that extends a class outside that tree, such as \RuntimeException, does not show the methods of that class.

SugarCraft\Animation

AnsiArt final class

A parsed .ansi ANSI-art document (the candy-top logo corpus format).

MethodSummary
static fromString(string $bytes): self
static fromFile(string $path): self
width(): intMax cell count over every row of every frame (half-blocks are single cells).
height(): intRow count of frame 0; redraw frames are assumed full-height by the corpus.
frameCount(): int
isAnimated(): bool
frameCells(int $frame): arrayRows of cells for one frame. Row lengths are kept NATURAL (ragged): trailing default-background spaces are absent in the corpus, and padding them would invent cells the artwork never painted.
sgrText(int $frame): stringRaw single-frame byte blob for apps that prefer replaying escapes verbatim instead of walking cells. Each cell carries a canonical WHOLE-state run, so a state change re-emits ESC[0m first (clearing components the next state omits) followed by the new canonical run; a change from default needs no reset, and each row plus the blob end in default state. The result is terminal-correct as replay AND cell-exactly re-parseable by fromString() — the accumulator reproduces every canonical whole-state run byte-for-byte, so the per-cell model and the raw stream stay in lockstep.

AnsiCell final class

One rendered terminal cell of a parsed .ansi artwork: the glyph plus the CANONICAL RESOLVED SGR state active for it — the full cumulative ECMA-48 style (attributes + foreground + background) a real terminal would be showing at that point, as a single ESC[…m run in the fixed order documented on AnsiArt::canonicalSgr(); '' when every component is at terminal default.

MethodSummary
static new(string $glyph, string $sgr = ''): selfHouse factory convention (::new()), mirroring the sugar-style immutable value-object shape.

ArtLibrary final class

Catalog over a directory of candy-top logo .ansi files, named logo-<slug>[-skinny][-anim]-<16|256|tc>-<WxH>.ansi.

MethodSummary
static fromDir(string $dir, bool $includeSkinny = false): selfIndex every matching art file in $dir. Unparsable names are skipped silently — a logo directory accumulates scratch files, and the catalog should degrade to the valid subset rather than fail the whole app.
static profileTag(ColorProfile $profile): stringMap a detected terminal colour profile onto this corpus's depth tags.
mergeManifest(string $jsonlPath): selfAttach per-slug description/tags from a logos.jsonl manifest. Tolerant by design: a missing/unreadable file or malformed rows is a no-op, because the manifest is optional human metadata shipped alongside the corpus, never a load-bearing dependency. The tolerance is paid with a bound — the read is capped at MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES, and a manifest beyond the gate is skipped exactly like an absent one (no throw, no partial enrichment, no unbounded slurp of a file we were going to distrust anyway).

description(string $slug): string

"preferred kind" is animation when $preferAnimated, else static. Returns null only when the slug is unknown entirely.

ArtLoop final class

Pure frame-pacing math for animated ANSI art. The .ansi corpus carries no per-frame delays (see AnsiArt), so playback speed is a caller policy: each frame shows for $frameSeconds, and the LAST frame is then held an extra $pauseSeconds before the loop restarts at frame 0 — the beat where the animation "breathes" on screen.

MethodSummary
static new(int $frameCount, float $frameSeconds = 0.1, float $pauseSeconds = 2.5): self
withPause(float $pauseSeconds): selfFluent pause variant — the dwell on the last frame is the usual tuning knob.
cycleSeconds(): floatOne full lap: every frame once, plus the closing hold on the last.
frameAt(float $elapsedSeconds): intWhich frame is on screen at an elapsed offset. Boundaries land on the later frame (a frame owns [start, start+duration) ).

Frame final class

One downsampled GIF frame. Stored as a 2-D grid of RGB triples or null (transparent) in cell-coordinate space (post-downsample). The Renderer walks the grid and emits ANSI escapes per cell.

MethodSummary
static new(array $cells, int $delay = 10, int $disposal = self::DISPOSAL_NONE, bool $transparent = false, ?string $rgba = null, int $rgbaWidth = 0, int $rgbaHeight = 0): selfMint a frame through the geometry door (SA-V1 -021): the optional RGBA triple must AGREE. The bare constructor let any caller pair a buffer with mismatched (or zero) dimensions, after which hasRgba() answered true for a lying geometry and every byte-length consumer inherited the lie. Bytes without dimensions, or dimensions without bytes, are the same contradiction read from the other side — both refuse at construction, so nothing downstream re-validates.
hasRgba(): boolWhether this frame carries the full-canvas RGBA capture (E-07).
rgbaBytes(): stringThe composited frame as packed RGBA bytes — row-major, 4 bytes per pixel, rgbaWidth() × rgbaHeight() pixels. This is the chicle-parity frame representation: lossless pixels, so a consumer can size its own output at print time instead of inheriting this decoder's grid.
rgbaWidth(): int
rgbaHeight(): int
width(): int
height(): int

Player final class

E-03: GIF player as a SugarCraft Model driven by an ABSOLUTE schedule. Loads every frame up-front (the decoder caps at 256); frame k is due at anchor + C[k] where C is the prefix sum of the frame periods (modulo one cycle of total length T), and each TickMsg re-arms the loop for the NEXT frame's deadline — max(nextDue - now, MIN_TICK_CS) — never a fresh copy of the CURRENT frame's delay. While the elapsed position resolves to a frame OTHER than the one on screen the table stays absolute from the kickoff origin: an overrun costs lateness, not drift, and the tick skips straight to its landing frame (the ArtLoop philosophy — on that path the displayed frame is a total function of elapsed time). The table DOES rescale at the wrap boundary, however: when the elapsed position lands back inside the window of the frame already on screen — which every stall of at least one full cycle does, as does a pump fired inside the current window — the tick force-advances exactly ONE frame and re-anchors the epoch to wall-clock now, so that frame holds a fresh full period. Post- wrap the cadence (the per-lap sequence of holds) is therefore preserved while the epoch is re-based, bounding the catch-up to one advance per tick. The naive alternative — continuing the absolute table without re- basing — was rejected because the force-advanced frame would survive only the sliver of window left before its table deadline (arbitrarily short partial holds at every stall boundary); the re-anchor is the shipped choice and PlayerScheduleTest pins the resulting index/arm stream against an independent walk. Before E-03 the Player re-armed the current frame's full delay on every tick, so the per-frame period was delay + handling + render time and playback silently stretched under load — the docblock here used to promise rate-stability the schedule did not deliver.

MethodSummary
__construct(public readonly array $frames, public readonly int $index = 0, public readonly bool $paused = false, public readonly string $preset = Renderer::PRESET_SOLID, public readonly ?Renderer $renderer = null, private readonly ?\Closure $now = null, public readonly ?float $fixedFps = null, public readonly ?float $maxSeconds = null, private readonly ?float $anchor = null, public readonly ?int $loops = null, private readonly int $lapsCarried = 0, private readonly ?\Closure $watch = null, private readonly float $elapsedCarried = 0.0, private readonly ?float $epochBasePos = null)The six seam parameters — $now, $anchor, $lapsCarried, $watch, $elapsedCarried, $epochBasePos — are internal wiring (test clock, schedule anchoring, lap carry across a reload, watch rebind, played-time carry across a re-anchor, the live epoch's establishment position), not caller vocabulary: hosts build Players via self::start() and the fluent setters, which thread the seams themselves. They stay public in the signature deliberately — promoted readonly state beats a parallel private-property ceremony — and the reload paths carry them via mutate().
init(): ?\Closure
update(Msg $msg): array
view(): string
withFixedFps(float $fps): selfE-09: override the per-frame GIF delays with a uniform cadence of $fps frames per second on the same absolute schedule. Immutable. Re-anchors the schedule to the currently shown frame so a mid-play switch never triggers an instant catch-up jump. Rates above self::MAX_FPS clamp to that advertised ceiling (chicle's CHICLE_ANIM_FPS_MAX): past the MIN_TICK_CS arm floor a faster request is indistinguishable from the ceiling, so the ceiling is made real rather than left a doc promise.
withMaxSeconds(float $seconds): selfE-09: stop playback once the schedule position (total play time; time spent paused never accrues) reaches $seconds. SA-P6 makes the "total" literal: every re-anchor — pause/resume, manual step, the early-fire force-advance, a cadence swap — folds its played segment into the elapsed carry the check compares (playSeconds()), so the bound can no longer be laundered by interacting with it. The bound lives in the model and is checked on each tick — no wall-clock timer is armed for it, so a stalled loop cannot overshoot silently either.
withLoops(?int $plays): selfE-02: cap playback at $plays total playthroughs (null = forever, the default). The stop happens INSIDE the schedule — on the tick whose position crosses the final lap boundary the Player returns Cmd::quit() while still displaying the last shown frame — so no wall-clock timer is armed for the bound (same E-09 law as withMaxSeconds()): a stalled loop cannot overshoot silently.
playOnce(): selfE-02: play the frame stream exactly once and quit. This is the honest counterpart of libnsgif's remark that "the only way to play the animation once is not to have this extension at all" (namzug16/libnsgif gif.c:862-871): because an unauthored stream reports infinite from Decoder::loopCount(), a host that wants one pass must ask the Player for it, not read it off the bytes.
withWatch(\Closure $probe): selfE-10: attach a watch probe. The closure is re-run every WATCH_POLL_SECONDS (see the constant's docblock for the chicle parity and the disclosed deviations); null = "no change", a frame list = "reload onto it now". Returns a new Player — the seam is state, not mutation.
withFrames(array $frames): selfE-10: rebind the playback to a different frame stream IN PLACE — the reload half of the watch cycle, exposed publicly so hosts can swap frames without rebuilding the Player. The position restarts (index 0, carried laps 0, epoch unanchored so the first tick of the new stream anchors by the E-03 next-arrival law); playback policy — preset, renderer, cadence, duration bound, loop bound, and the watch seam itself — survives. A caller that wants the loop bound re-derived from the new bytes chains withLoops() onto the result. The asymmetry is the contract: the manual swap keeps the caller's bound because only the caller knows its intent, while the WatchMsg reload in self::update() re-derives the bound from the fresh bytes on purpose, so a file whose loop extension changed mid-session gets its new bound without the caller lifting a finger (pinned by PlayerWatchTest). SA-P6: the duration bound rides this survive-list as a carried total too — the live segment folds into the elapsed carry before the epoch drops, so swapping streams mid-run is not a budget reset either.
subscriptions(): ?\SugarCraft\Core\Subscriptions
playedSeconds(): ?floatE-09: the duration bound measured so far ON THE CURRENT SCHEDULE (null before the schedule is anchored, i.e. before the first tick) — the raw epoch position the E-03 cadence pins observe. The maxSeconds BOUND proper measures total play time across re-anchors — see self::playSeconds(); SA-P6 fixed that bound to carry, not this accessor.

TickMsg final class

Per-frame animation tick driving the sugar-animation image transition.

WatchMsg final class

E-10: One poll of the Player watch seam. Armed by the Player itself (init and every completed poll re-arm it at WATCH_POLL_SECONDS), consumed by Player::update() — the sugar-animation twin of chicle's run_watch re-stat cycle (tools/chafa/chafa.c:896-940), lifted from a g_usleep busy-loop into the event loop the TEA runtime already owns.
